# required-headings

- ID: `MD043`
- Category: Headings
- Default: on, severity warning
- Fixable: no
- Tags: `headings`

Headings follow the configured outline in order. No outline is set by default.

## Why

Projects can require a set of similar documents, such as runbooks, to share one
structure.

## Options

Set them under `rules.required-headings.options`.

- `headings` (`string[]`, default `[]`): Headings the document must have, in
  order, such as \#\# Usage. \* stands for any number of headings, \+ for one or
  more, and ? for exactly one.
- `match_case` (`boolean`, default `false`): Compare the text of headings in the
  same case.

## Fix

There is no automatic fix. Only the author can write the missing sections.

## Example

With this configuration:

```yaml
rules:
  required-headings:
    options:
      headings:
        - "# Guide"
        - "## Install"
        - "## Usage"
```

This document breaks the rule:

```markdown
# Guide

## Usage

Run the tool in the project root.
```

gomdlint reports:

```text
3:1 Expected heading "## Install", found "## Usage"
```

This document follows the rule:

```markdown
# Guide

## Install

Run the installer.

## Usage

Run the tool in the project root.
```

## Configure

```yaml
rules:
  required-headings:
    options:
      headings: []
```

Under `rules`, `required-headings: false` turns the rule off and
`required-headings: error` reports its findings as errors. The flag
`--disable required-headings` turns it off for one run.

## Silence one line

```markdown
<!-- markdownlint-disable-next-line required-headings -->
```
